space_groups.source: CLDR main/ar.xml groups digits with a mark, not a space.

plural_scale_needs_count.source: CLDR RBNF, common/rbnf/ar.xml (unicode-org/cldr, cldrVersion 50): "3000: << آلاف": the plural takes a count from 3 to 10.

scale_noun_agrees.source: CLDR RBNF, common/rbnf/ar.xml (unicode-org/cldr, cldrVersion 50): "2000000: <%%spellout-numbering-m< مليون": the singular مليون follows a count above two ("أحد عشر مليونا", "مائة مليون"); the plural ملايين after 3 to 10 is one more form, not a rule that the singular takes only one.

joiner_tens_units.source: CLDR RBNF, common/rbnf/ar.xml (unicode-org/cldr, cldrVersion 50): "20: [>> و]عشرون": the unit, و, then the ten ("خمسة وعشرون").

joiner_after_hundred.source: CLDR RBNF, common/rbnf/ar.xml (unicode-org/cldr, cldrVersion 50): "100: مائة[ و>>]".

joiner_between_groups.source: CLDR RBNF, common/rbnf/ar.xml (unicode-org/cldr, cldrVersion 50): "1000: ألف[ و>>]".

joiner_before_round_hundred.source: CLDR RBNF, common/rbnf/ar.xml (unicode-org/cldr, cldrVersion 50): "1000: ألف[ و>>]": و goes before any rest after a thousand, a round hundred too ("ألف وخمسمائة").

tens_order.source: CLDR RBNF, common/rbnf/ar.xml (unicode-org/cldr, cldrVersion 50): "20: [>> و]عشرون"; Karin C. Ryding, A Reference Grammar of Modern Standard Arabic (Cambridge, 2005), chapter 15 "Numerals and numeral constructions": units precede tens.

ordinal_style.source: CLDR RBNF, common/rbnf/ar.xml (unicode-org/cldr, cldrVersion 50), spellout-ordinal-masculine: "11: الحادي عشر", "21: >%%ordinal-ones-masculine> والعشرون": the ordinal unit, then the cardinal teen word or ten.

half_of_scale.source: Karin C. Ryding, A Reference Grammar of Modern Standard Arabic (Cambridge, 2005), chapter 15 "Numerals and numeral constructions": "ونصف" after a number adds half of its last unit; "ألف ونصف" is 1500.

fold_marks.source: Karin C. Ryding, A Reference Grammar of Modern Standard Arabic (Cambridge, 2005), chapter 15 "Numerals and numeral constructions": short-vowel marks (harakat), shadda and tanwin are mostly left out in writing; hamza on alif (أ إ آ) is often left out too. None of them changes which number a word names.

kept_marks.source: Karin C. Ryding, A Reference Grammar of Modern Standard Arabic (Cambridge, 2005), chapter 15 "Numerals and numeral constructions": hamza (ء) is a consonant; on alif it is written with the letter (أ إ آ). A word with its hamza is a different word from a word without it: "وأحد" (and + one, in "مئة وأحد عشر") is not "واحد" (one).

letter_folds.source: Arabic writing often puts ي for final ى and ه for final ة ("احدي", "ثلاثه"), and stretches words with tatweel (ـ); these read the same.

bidi_controls.source: CLDR main/ar.xml writes the latn minus sign as "\u200e-": directional marks stand next to numbers in right-to-left text.

native_digits.source: CLDR common/supplemental/numberingSystems.xml: arab digits ٠-٩ (U+0660-U+0669), the native digits of ar, and arabext ۰-۹; CLDR root arab symbols: decimal "٫" (U+066B), group "٬" (U+066C).

clitic_min_rest.source: A single-letter preposition (ب, ل, ك) comes off only before a word of three letters or more, so that "لست" ("I am not") stays a word.

joiner_prefix.source: Karin C. Ryding, A Reference Grammar of Modern Standard Arabic (Cambridge, 2005), chapter 15 "Numerals and numeral constructions": the conjunction wa- is written joined to the next word ("وعشرون").

clitic_prefix.source: Karin C. Ryding, A Reference Grammar of Modern Standard Arabic (Cambridge, 2005), chapter 15 "Numerals and numeral constructions": the article al- and the prepositions bi-, li-, ka- are written joined to the next word ("الثالث", "بخمسة").

decimal_marker.source: CLDR RBNF, common/rbnf/ar.xml (unicode-org/cldr, cldrVersion 50): "x.x: << فاصل >>"; "فاصلة" (comma) is the common spoken form.

minus.source: CLDR RBNF, common/rbnf/ar.xml (unicode-org/cldr, cldrVersion 50): "-x: ناقص >>"; "سالب" (negative) also marks a negative number.

range_cue.source: Karin C. Ryding, A Reference Grammar of Modern Standard Arabic (Cambridge, 2005), chapter 15 "Numerals and numeral constructions": "بين", between; in "بين ألف وألفين" the joined و links the two limits.
